hello.note: Also very common: السلام عليكم (es-salamu 'aleikom); reply وعليكم السلام (wa 'aleikom es-salam).

please.note: To a woman: men fadlek (same spelling). Just as common: لو سمحت (law samaht).

thank_you.note: Thanks a lot: متشكر أوي (motashakker awi); a woman says متشكرة (motashakkera).

youre_welcome.note: Very Egyptian: على إيه؟ ('ala eh?), literally 'for what?'

no.note: Ends in a sharp catch in the throat, unlike standard لا (la).

sorry.note: A woman says: آسفة (asfa). For small slips Egyptians often say معلش (ma'lesh).

excuse_me.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

good_morning.note: Reply: صباح النور (sabah en-nur), 'morning of light'.

how_are_you.note: To a woman: ezzay hadretek? (same spelling). Casual: إزيك؟ (ezzayak?), to a woman ezzayek?

im_fine.note: A woman says: كويسة (kwayyesa). Egyptians thank God here rather than the person asking.

whats_your_name.note: To a woman: esm hadretek eh? (same spelling). Casual: اسمك إيه؟ (esmak eh?)

nice_to_meet_you.note: Reply: وأنا أسعد (w ana as'ad), 'and I'm happier'.

where_from.note: To a woman: hadretek menein? (same spelling). Casual: إنت منين؟ (enta menein?)

speak_english.note: To a woman: حضرتك بتتكلمي إنجليزي؟ (hadretek betetkallemi engelizi?)

dont_understand.note: A woman says: مش فاهمة (mesh fahma).

speak_slowly.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي، اتكلمي بالراحة شوية (law samahti, etkallemi berraha shwayya).

how_much.note: For a feminine item: دي بكام؟ (di bekam?)

where_bathroom.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

can_you_help.note: To a woman: ممكن تساعديني؟ (momken tesa'dini?)

what_means.note: About a word: الكلمة دي يعني إيه؟ (el-kelma di ya'ni eh?)

one.note: Written ١. Egyptian prices, signs and number plates use these Eastern Arabic digits.

five.note: Written ٥, which looks like a zero; zero itself is a dot (٠).

eight.note: Written ٨, an upside-down V: don't mix it up with ٧ (seven).

water.note: A bottle of water: إزازة ميّة (ezazet mayya).

coffee.note: Say how sweet: سادة (sada) no sugar, مظبوط (mazbut) medium, زيادة (zeyada) sweet.

bread.note: Egyptians say عيش ('eish), which also means 'life', not the standard خبز.

im_hungry.note: A woman says: أنا جعانة (ana ga'ana).

menu_please.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

bill_please.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

delicious.note: Very Egyptian: تحفة! (tohfa!), literally 'a masterpiece'. Of a feminine dish: طعمها (ta'maha).

no_meat.note: لحمة means red meat; to rule out chicken add ولا فراخ (wala ferakh). Vegetarian: نباتي (nabati).

straight_ahead.note: Also means 'right away' or 'always', depending on context.

stop_here.note: Taxi classic: على جنب يا أسطى ('ala gamb ya osta), 'pull over, driver'.

airport.note: To a taxi driver: على المطار ('ala el-matar), 'to the airport'.

train_station.note: Cairo's main station is called محطة مصر (mahattet masr).

want_to_go.note: A woman says: عايزة أروح … ('ayza aruh …).

is_it_far.note: For a feminine place: هي بعيدة؟ (heyya be'ida?)

one_ticket.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

too_expensive.note: For a feminine item: دي غالية أوي (di ghalya awi). Haggling: كتير أوي (ketir awi), 'that's too much'.

cheaper.note: Also: عندك حاجة أرخص؟ ('andak haga arkhas?)

id_like_this.note: A woman says: عايزة ('ayza). For a feminine item use دي (di) instead of ده (da).

pay_card.note: Egyptians call any bank card فيزا (fiza). Also: بالكارت (bel-kart).

closed.note: Printed signs usually say مغلق (moghlaq), but in speech it's مقفول.

later.note: In a little while: بعد شوية (ba'd shwayya).

good_night.note: To a woman: تصبحي على خير (tesbahi 'ala kheir). Reply: وإنت من أهله (w enta men ahlo).

see_you_later.note: To a woman: ashufek ba'dein (same spelling).

wait_moment.note: To a woman: استني لحظة، لو سمحتي (estanni lahza, law samahti). Also: ثانية واحدة (sanya wahda).

help.note: The Egyptian cry for help, literally 'come to my aid!'. To one man: الحقني! (elha'ni!)

call_police.note: To one man: اطلب البوليس! (otlob el-bolis!). Police emergency number in Egypt: 122.

need_doctor.note: A woman says: أنا محتاجة دكتور (ana mehtaga doktor).

im_lost.note: A woman says: أنا تايهة (ana tayha).

dont_feel_well.note: A woman says: مش حاسة إني كويسة (mesh hassa enni kwayyesa). Also: أنا تعبان (ana ta'ban).

lost_phone.note: If it was stolen: موبايلي اتسرق (mobayli etsara').

be_careful.note: To a woman: khalli balek! (same spelling). For sudden danger: حاسب! (haseb!)

no_problem.note: Also: ولا يهمك (wala yhemmak), 'don't worry about it'.

dont_like_it.note: For a feminine noun: مش عاجباني (mesh 'agbani).

im_tired.note: A woman says: أنا تعبانة (ana ta'bana). Can also mean 'I'm unwell'.

im_happy.note: A woman says: أنا مبسوطة (ana mabsuta).

welcome.note: Very Egyptian: نورت! (nawwart!), 'you've lit up the place'; to a woman nawwarti.

congratulations.note: Reply: الله يبارك فيك (allah yebarek fik).

my_family.note: Also: أسرتي (osreti), a bit more formal.

mother.note: Your own mum: ماما (mama). Respectfully: الوالدة (el-walda).

father.note: Your own dad: بابا (baba). Respectfully: الوالد (el-waled).

child.note: That's a son; a daughter is بنت (bent). My children: أولادي (awladi).

friend.note: Female: صاحبة (sahba). More formal: صديق (sadi'), صديقة (sadi'a).

this_is_my_friend.note: Female friend: دي صاحبتي (di sahbeti); a man may say صديقتي (sadi'ti) to avoid 'girlfriend'.

are_you_married.note: To a woman: حضرتك متجوزة؟ (hadretek metgawweza?)

have_children.note: To a woman: hadretek 'andek awlad? (same spelling).

monday.note: Same word as 'two' (etnein): the week is counted from Sunday.

friday.note: The weekly prayer day and Egypt's main day off.

weekend.note: Borrowed from English and widely used. In Egypt the weekend is Friday and Saturday.

fifteen.note: Written ١٥. The numbers 13 to 19 all end in -tashar.

fifty.note: Written ٥٠. Fifty pounds: خمسين جنيه (khamsin geneh).

hundred.note: Written ١٠٠. Before a noun it shortens: مية جنيه (meet geneh), 100 pounds.

how_old.note: To a woman: 'omr hadretek kam? (same spelling). Casual: عمرك كام؟ ('omrak kam?)

years_old.note: With 3 to 10 the word becomes سنين (senin).

what_colour.note: For a feminine noun: لونها إيه؟ (lonha eh?)

that_one.note: Egyptian uses ده for both 'this' and 'that'. Feminine: اللي هناك دي (elli henak di).

another_one.note: For a feminine item: واحدة كمان (wahda kaman). To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

its_hot.note: Literally 'the world is hot'. Also: الجو حر (eg-gaww harr).

its_cold.note: I'm cold: أنا بردان (ana bardan); a woman says بردانة (bardana).

its_windy.note: Strong wind: في هوا جامد (fi hawa gamed).

umbrella.note: The same word means a sunshade or beach parasol.

winter.note: In Egypt شتا (shita) also means rain.

have_reservation.note: Add the name: باسم (besm) + your name.

room.note: Hotel signs use the standard غرفة (ghorfa).

luggage.note: One bag: شنطة (shanta). At the airport also: العفش (el-'afsh).

wifi_password.note: Also: الباسورد بتاع الواي فاي إيه؟ (el-baswerd beta' el-wai fai eh?)

check_out_time.note: Also: لازم أسيب الأوضة الساعة كام؟ (lazem asib el-oda es-sa'a kam?)

next_train.note: Also: القطر الجاي الساعة كام؟ (el-'atr eg-gai es-sa'a kam?)

is_this_seat_free.note: Also: في حد قاعد هنا؟ (fi had 'a'ed hena?), 'is anyone sitting here?'

what_do_you_do.note: To a woman: حضرتك بتشتغلي إيه؟ (hadretek beteshtaghali eh?)

i_work_in.note: E.g. في بنك (fi bank), في السياحة (fes-seyaha) in tourism.

im_student.note: A woman says: أنا طالبة (ana talba).

meeting.note: In offices you'll also hear ميتنج (miting).

im_busy.note: A woman says: أنا مشغولة (ana mashghula).

day_off.note: Also means a holiday or vacation. I'm off today: النهارده أجازة (en-naharda agaza).

good_job.note: To a woman: برافو عليكي (brafo 'aleiki). Slang: عاش! ('ash!)

table_for_two.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

what_recommend.note: To a woman: حضرتك تنصحيني بإيه؟ (hadretek tensahini b-eh?)

not_spicy.note: Spicy-hot is حرّاق (harra'). To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

vegetarian_food.note: I'm vegetarian: أنا نباتي (ana nabati); a woman says نباتية (nabateyya).

more_water.note: To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

no_sugar.note: For coffee Egyptians just say سادة (sada), 'plain'.

im_full.note: When offered more, Egyptians say الحمد لله (el-hamdu lellah).

takeaway.note: Egyptians use the English 'take away'. To a woman: لو سمحتي (law samahti).

it_was_delicious.note: To the cook: تسلم إيدك (teslam idak), 'bless your hands'; to a woman: teslam idek.

keep_change.note: To a woman: khalli el-ba'i 'ashanek (same spelling).

stomach.note: Doctors say معدة (me'da) for the stomach itself.

head_hurts.note: Also: عندي صداع ('andi soda'), 'I have a headache'.

call_ambulance.note: To one man: اطلب الإسعاف! (otlob el-es'af!). Ambulance number in Egypt: 123.

dentist.note: Also: دكتور أسنان (doktor asnan). A woman dentist: دكتورة (doktora).

need_rest.note: A woman says: أنا محتاجة أرتاح (ana mehtaga artah).

feel_better.note: Also: أحسن، الحمد لله (ahsan, el-hamdu lellah).

get_well.note: To a woman: salamtek! (same spelling). Reply: الله يسلمك (allah yesallemak).

lets_meet.note: When shall we meet? نتقابل إمتى؟ (net'abel emta?)

are_you_free.note: To a woman: حضرتك فاضية بكرة؟ (hadretek fadya bokra?)

call_me.note: To a woman: ابقي كلميني (eb'i kallemini). ابقى (eb'a) softens it: 'do call me'.

your_number.note: To a woman: ra'am hadretek kam? (same spelling). Casual: نمرتك كام؟ (nemretak kam?)

have_nice_day.note: To a woman: naharek sa'id! (same spelling). Also used as a greeting.

good_luck.note: Also: ربنا معاك (rabbena ma'ak), 'God be with you'; to a woman: معاكي (ma'aki).

happy_birthday.note: To a woman: كل سنة وإنتي طيبة (koll sana w enti tayyeba). Also said on holidays.

thanks_a_lot.note: A woman says: متشكرة أوي (motashakkera awi). Also: ألف شكر (alf shokr).

miss_you.note: To a woman: وحشتيني (wahashtini), stressing the long 'ti'. So much: وحشتني أوي (wahashtini awi).
